source.notes: data/terrain.py: no downloaded PGDA 5 m tile covers this point, so LOLA 120 m is used from the site out: rays at 0.5 deg azimuth along great circles, 5 m steps to 12 km, 60 m steps to 300 km, exact sphere geometry (curvature included). Observer 2 m above ground 1812.5 m (LOLA, bilinear). DEM is MOON_ME (DE421); the site lat/lon is taken as the same frame as Horizons (risk R3).

uncertainty.summary: LOLA 120 m only: features smaller than ~120 m, including those next to the antenna, are smoothed away, and with no 5 m tile here there is no height-error estimate. A nearby rock or rise can raise the true horizon above this one.

The terrain horizon in this file comes from DEMs in MOON_ME (DE421): the two lunar frames differ slightly, and the site lat/lon is taken as the same in both (risk R3).

uncertainty.summary: Apparent az/el (light-time and aberration corrected), not geometric, and no terrain (data/horizons.py observer_table shortcut). Horizons gives no formal az/el uncertainty, so the error here is unknown. angularRadiusDeg is one value at the mean Sun range (data/sites.py shortcut); the true radius varies over the window.
